steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Convolutional layers apply learned filters across an image to detect local patterns.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Other architectures can also process images; the question asks specifically about convolutional filters.

challenges.title: Reusing a pretrained encoder
challenges.description: You have a small labeled image dataset and a pretrained image encoder. Which is a transfer-learning approach?

choices.text: Assume the pretrained model is accurate without evaluating it.
Use the pretrained encoder's features and train a task-specific classifier.
Discard all pretrained weights and claim no prior learning was used.
Train on the final test labels to improve the encoder.

challenges.hint: Reuse a representation learned from an earlier task.

solution.code: Use the pretrained encoder's features and train a task-specific classifier.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: A pretrained encoder can supply representations for a new classifier.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: The adapted system still needs evaluation on held-out examples from the new task.

challenges.title: Attention in language models
challenges.description: In a transformer, what does an attention mechanism let a token representation use?

choices.text: The correct answer from an unseen test set.
A guarantee that generated statements are true.
A weighted combination of information from permitted tokens in the context.
Only the token's position, with no information from other tokens.

challenges.hint: Consider how the model relates tokens within a context.

solution.code: A weighted combination of information from permitted tokens in the context.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Attention weights determine how information from allowed tokens contributes to a representation.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Attention masks can restrict which tokens are permitted, such as future tokens in a causal language model.

challenges.title: Pixels or boxes?
challenges.description: A vision system must assign a class to each pixel in an image. Which task is this?

choices.text: Object detection using only bounding boxes.
Image-level classification with one label for the whole image.
Predicting a single numeric price.
Semantic segmentation.

challenges.hint: The required output has a label at every pixel.

solution.code: Semantic segmentation.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Semantic segmentation assigns a semantic class to each pixel.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Object detection typically identifies objects with bounding boxes rather than labeling every pixel.

challenges.title: Reward and behavior
challenges.description: A reinforcement learning agent receives reward for collecting points but is never penalized for damaging equipment. What risk follows from this reward design?

choices.text: The agent may learn to collect points while damaging equipment.
The agent will automatically infer every unstated safety goal.
The reward guarantees safe behavior.
The task has become supervised classification.

challenges.hint: The agent optimizes the feedback it receives, not an unstated objective.

solution.code: The agent may learn to collect points while damaging equipment.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: A policy can exploit the specified reward while ignoring an omitted cost.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Safety requirements need explicit design and evaluation; adding a penalty alone is not a guarantee.

challenges.title: Plausible generated text
challenges.description: A generative model produces a fluent answer containing a specific historical claim. What should you infer from fluency alone?

choices.text: The model has permission to reproduce any source.
The claim needs verification; fluent text can still be false.
The claim is verified because the text is grammatical.
The model retrieved an authoritative source.

challenges.hint: Distinguish plausible language from evidence.

solution.code: The claim needs verification; fluent text can still be false.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: A generative model can produce convincing but incorrect statements.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Factual accuracy and permission to reuse content require separate checks.

challenges.title: Grounding an answer
challenges.description: An assistant must answer questions about an organization's frequently updated policy documents. Which design can supply current document context at answer time?

choices.text: Disable access to the documents and ask the model to guess.
Use the user's question as proof of the policy.
Retrieve relevant current documents and include them in the model's context.
Assume the model's original training always contains the latest policy.

challenges.hint: Provide the model with relevant external information when the question is asked.

solution.code: Retrieve relevant current documents and include them in the model's context.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Retrieval can bring current source passages into the prompt.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: The answer should still be checked against the retrieved sources; retrieval can return irrelevant or stale material.

challenges.title: Monitoring after deployment
challenges.description: A model is deployed for loan applications. Why monitor both input data and model outcomes over time?

choices.text: Monitoring guarantees that the model is fair.
Monitoring makes model versions unnecessary.
Training metrics automatically update when production data changes.
Input or outcome changes can reveal drift or performance problems.

challenges.hint: Production data can differ from the data used for training.

solution.code: Input or outcome changes can reveal drift or performance problems.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Changes in inputs and observed outcomes can signal that the model needs investigation.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: A drift signal does not by itself prove a loss of predictive performance or identify its cause.

challenges.title: Data-parallel training
challenges.description: In synchronous data-parallel training, what do workers typically do before a shared parameter update?

choices.text: Compute gradients on different data batches and aggregate them.
Train unrelated models without sharing any gradients.
Use only the final test set as their training data.
Delete the model parameters on every device.

challenges.hint: The same model is trained across different portions of the data.

solution.code: Compute gradients on different data batches and aggregate them.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Each worker computes gradients for its batch, and the gradients are combined.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Communication and synchronization can limit the speedup from adding devices.

challenges.title: Evaluating AutoML
challenges.description: An AutoML system selects a model after trying many configurations. How should you assess its final performance?

choices.text: Skip evaluation because the search was automated.
Evaluate the selected model on a test set not used in the search.
Report the best search score as an unbiased final test score.
Select the model using the final test set repeatedly.

challenges.hint: Automation does not remove selection bias.

solution.code: Evaluate the selected model on a test set not used in the search.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: A separate test set provides a final check after automated model selection.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Trying many configurations can overfit the validation data used by the search.

challenges.title: Learning from a graph
challenges.description: What does a graph neural network commonly use to update a node's representation?

choices.text: A requirement that nodes have no edges.
The final test set's target values.
Information aggregated from its neighboring nodes.
Only a random new label assigned to every node.

challenges.hint: Consider what the graph's edges connect.

solution.code: Information aggregated from its neighboring nodes.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Message-passing layers combine information from a node and its neighborhood.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: The aggregation follows the available graph structure and must avoid leaking unavailable information.

challenges.title: A missing modality
challenges.description: An image-and-text model normally receives a photo and a caption. What is a useful evaluation for deployment?

choices.text: Test only cases with identical correct inputs.
Assume either modality can never fail.
Use the correct answer as a hidden input.
Test cases where the image or caption is missing or misleading.

challenges.hint: Real inputs may be incomplete or disagree.

solution.code: Test cases where the image or caption is missing or misleading.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Missing and conflicting inputs test how the system behaves when modalities are unreliable.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Performance on complete, consistent inputs does not establish robustness to those cases.

challenges.title: Reducing model size
challenges.description: What does model quantization typically change to reduce memory use?

choices.text: It represents weights or activations with lower numerical precision.
It adds more training examples to the dataset.
It replaces evaluation with a smaller test set.
It guarantees identical predictions for all inputs.

challenges.hint: Think about the number of bits used to store numbers.

solution.code: It represents weights or activations with lower numerical precision.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Lower-precision representations can reduce model memory and sometimes improve inference speed.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: Quantization can affect accuracy, so the optimized model must be measured.

challenges.title: Responding to unequal errors
challenges.description: A loan model has a substantially higher false-negative rate for one group. What is an appropriate next step?

choices.text: Assume a single metric proves the cause of the disparity.
Investigate the disparity, its impact, and possible mitigations with affected stakeholders.
Conclude that the model is fair because overall accuracy is high.
Hide subgroup results and deploy unchanged.

challenges.hint: An aggregate score can conceal differences in errors.

solution.code: Investigate the disparity, its impact, and possible mitigations with affected stakeholders.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Subgroup error rates can reveal unequal outcomes that warrant further analysis.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: A disparity alone does not establish its cause or identify the best mitigation.

challenges.title: Closing the production loop
challenges.description: After deploying a model, what helps a team detect degradation and decide whether to update it?

choices.text: Retrain automatically on every new label without checks.
Remove model version records to simplify operations.
Monitor inputs and outcomes, then investigate and evaluate changes before release.
Assume the original test score applies forever.

challenges.hint: The lifecycle continues after the first deployment.

solution.code: Monitor inputs and outcomes, then investigate and evaluate changes before release.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.explanation: Monitoring and feedback provide evidence for investigating changes in performance.

steps.title: Check the distinction
steps.explanation: A proposed update still needs validation and a controlled release.

challenges.title: Testing position robustness in images
challenges.description: A CNN performs well when a defect is centered but often misses the same defect near image borders. What is a useful next step?

choices.text: Add representative position-shifted training examples and evaluate performance across image locations.
Relabel border defects as background.
Sort pixels by brightness before inference.
Measure only centered examples because the model is convolutional.

challenges.hint: Check whether training and evaluation cover the positions seen in deployment.

solution.code: Add representative position-shifted training examples and evaluate performance across image locations.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A model can still fail on locations underrepresented in its examples.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Position-shifted data and location-specific evaluation test whether the system handles defects across the frame.

challenges.title: Relating distant sequence elements
challenges.description: A document classifier must detect when a phrase near the end changes the meaning of a term near the beginning. Which property is useful?

choices.text: A two-token convolution guarantees access to the whole document.
Attention can let a token representation use information from distant permitted tokens.
A bag of token counts preserves every word-order relationship.
Reading only the first token captures every later dependency.

challenges.hint: Consider how information travels between far-apart sequence positions.

solution.code: Attention can let a token representation use information from distant permitted tokens.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: The relevant evidence may be far apart, so a strictly local operation alone is insufficient.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Self-attention forms context-aware representations using information from other allowed positions.

challenges.title: Preserving temporal order
challenges.description: A sensor model receives a variable-length sequence of hourly readings and must use earlier readings in order. Which model family fits temporal patterns?

choices.text: An image CNN applied after sorting readings by value.
A lookup table indexed only by sequence length.
A recurrent neural network that updates its state as it processes the sequence.
A model that replaces every sequence with its mean.

challenges.hint: Look for a model that carries information forward through an ordered series.

solution.code: A recurrent neural network that updates its state as it processes the sequence.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Sorting or averaging discards timing order the task needs.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A recurrent model processes readings in sequence and maintains a state summarizing earlier inputs.

challenges.title: Matching architecture to modality
challenges.description: A team has photographs, text messages, and equipment time series. Which initial plan matches the course guidance?

choices.text: Use one recurrent model for every input because all data can be serialized.
Use CNNs only for text and lookup tables for images.
Choose the architecture with the most parameters without a baseline.
Compare CNNs for images, transformers for text sequences, and recurrent models for temporal patterns.

challenges.hint: Match the model family to the structure represented by each input.

solution.code: Compare CNNs for images, transformers for text sequences, and recurrent models for temporal patterns.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Images have spatial neighborhoods, text has token relationships, and sensor series have temporal order.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: These model families exploit different structures, but choices still need empirical validation.

challenges.title: Testing architecture against a baseline
challenges.description: A transformer scores slightly better than a small CNN on a tiny image dataset but serves much slower. What comparison is sound?

choices.text: Measure both on the same held-out data and compare quality and latency against a simple baseline.
Select the transformer because newer architectures are always better.
Compare training accuracy only and ignore deployment cost.
Increase the test set until it favors the transformer.

challenges.hint: Assess success using prediction quality and operational constraints.

solution.code: Measure both on the same held-out data and compare quality and latency against a simple baseline.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A small apparent gain is not decisive if measured inconsistently or without latency.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A common held-out comparison against a baseline reveals whether extra complexity is worthwhile.

challenges.title: Handling sequence position
challenges.description: A text model receives the same words in two different orders, and order can change intent. Why preserve sequence position?

choices.text: Position makes every token independently correct.
The model must distinguish token relationships that depend on order.
Shuffled tokens always retain the original meaning.
Position is a substitute for checking model outputs.

challenges.hint: Ask whether meaning changes when token order changes.

solution.code: The model must distinguish token relationships that depend on order.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: An unordered representation would treat some distinct sequences as equivalent.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Position-aware sequence processing supplies information needed to learn order-sensitive patterns.

challenges.title: Choosing under a latency budget
challenges.description: A recurrent model meets a strict response-time limit; a larger attention model has a modest validation gain but misses the limit. What is supported?

choices.text: Deploy the attention model because validation quality always overrides the limit.
Remove latency from acceptance criteria.
Keep the feasible model or seek a measured optimization before adopting the slower model.
Assume batching makes response-time limits irrelevant.

challenges.hint: Apply the stated deployment constraint as part of model selection.

solution.code: Keep the feasible model or seek a measured optimization before adopting the slower model.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A model that misses a required response time is not successful as configured.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Prefer a measured feasible baseline unless optimization restores latency without unacceptable quality loss.

challenges.title: Preventing target-set leakage during adaptation
challenges.description: A transfer-learning team adapts a pretrained encoder using every target-domain image, including images later called the final test set. Which protocol supports a credible final estimate?

choices.text: Use the test images for adaptation but hide their labels.
Choose the final model by repeatedly checking the test score.
Report the training score as the target-domain estimate.
Reserve the final test examples before any adaptation choices, and use only training or validation data for those choices.

challenges.hint: Keep the final test set outside the full model-selection and adaptation process.

solution.code: Reserve the final test examples before any adaptation choices, and use only training or validation data for those choices.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Using test examples to adapt representations lets information from the evaluation set influence the model.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Hold out final test examples before adaptation, then evaluate once after selecting the approach.

challenges.title: Unfreezing after a frozen baseline
challenges.description: A frozen encoder performs poorly on a new microscopy domain, though images contain recognizable objects. What next experiment is informative?

choices.text: Unfreeze selected later encoder layers and compare fine-tuning with the frozen baseline.
Unfreeze no layers but report training score as adaptation.
Fine-tune on test examples.
Change class names while keeping the weights fixed.

challenges.hint: Test whether limited weight adaptation can bridge domain differences.

solution.code: Unfreeze selected later encoder layers and compare fine-tuning with the frozen baseline.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Poor frozen-feature performance suggests the pretrained representation may not fit the new visual domain.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Selective unfreezing tests adaptation while retaining pretrained features; compare on untouched validation data.

challenges.title: Recognizing transfer domain mismatch
challenges.description: A natural-image encoder transfers poorly to grayscale medical scans despite correct labels and preprocessing. What conclusion is defensible?

choices.text: The poor score proves the labels are wrong.
Source and target domains may differ enough that transferred features need adaptation and careful evaluation.
Pretraining guarantees strong performance on any image domain.
Add test examples to training until the score rises.

challenges.hint: Separate the value of pretraining from the match between source and target data.

solution.code: Source and target domains may differ enough that transferred features need adaptation and careful evaluation.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Different image domains can expose features that do not transfer directly.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Try controlled fine-tuning or a more relevant representation and keep evaluation data separate.

challenges.title: Keeping preprocessing consistent
challenges.description: A pretrained encoder expects normalized RGB images, but its classifier trains on raw pixels and serves on normalized pixels. What is likely?

choices.text: Normalization changes class labels automatically.
The encoder infers missing training normalization from test data.
Training and serving inputs differ, so the classifier may behave unreliably.
Different scales guarantee better transfer.

challenges.hint: Compare the representation during adaptation with inference.

solution.code: Training and serving inputs differ, so the classifier may behave unreliably.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A mismatch in input scaling creates train-serve inconsistency even with unchanged weights.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Use consistent documented preprocessing in training, validation, and deployment.

challenges.title: Detecting overfit during fine-tuning
challenges.description: A fine-tuned model reaches near-perfect training accuracy on 120 examples while validation accuracy falls each epoch. What is appropriate?

choices.text: Continue training because training accuracy is decisive.
Use validation examples for gradient updates until their score rises.
Conclude the pretrained encoder is defective.
Treat the train-validation gap as overfitting and reduce adaptation or add justified regularization.

challenges.hint: Compare training fit with performance on held-out examples.

solution.code: Treat the train-validation gap as overfitting and reduce adaptation or add justified regularization.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Strong training performance with declining validation performance indicates poor generalization.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Try fewer unfrozen layers or earlier stopping; choose settings with validation, not test data.

challenges.title: Adapting the output to target labels
challenges.description: An image encoder trained to identify animals is adapted for four crop-disease labels. What must be true of its prediction output after adaptation?

choices.text: Its output mapping must represent the four crop-disease labels, whether the existing head is retrained or a new one is used.
Keep the animal classes and reinterpret their scores as crop diseases.
Change input normalization while leaving the animal output meanings unchanged.
Use hidden encoder features as disease decisions without mapping them to target labels.

challenges.hint: Focus on what each output means, not whether a particular layer is replaced.

solution.code: Its output mapping must represent the four crop-disease labels, whether the existing head is retrained or a new one is used.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: The encoder may provide reusable image features, but its original output meanings refer to animal categories.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Train or configure the output mapping for the four target labels, then evaluate it on held-out crop images.

challenges.title: Handling rare words with subword tokens
challenges.description: A tokenizer encounters product codes it has never seen as whole words. Why can subword tokenization help?

choices.text: It guarantees every code has a meaningful pretrained definition.
It can represent an unseen whole word as smaller known pieces.
It removes the need to inspect important identifier splits.
It converts text sequences into image pixels.

challenges.hint: Consider what happens when the complete string is absent from the vocabulary.

solution.code: It can represent an unseen whole word as smaller known pieces.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Breaking a string into familiar pieces can reduce the out-of-vocabulary problem.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Pieces may still be unhelpful, so inspect tokenization and evaluate on the domain.

challenges.title: Checking tokenization boundaries
challenges.description: A legal classifier misses decisions where section numbers and hyphenated terms matter. What should the team inspect first?

choices.text: Whether the model uses more image augmentation.
Whether test labels are converted into pixel masks.
Whether the tokenizer preserves or splits those domain-specific strings usefully.
Whether the model has a larger reward per prediction.

challenges.hint: Look at how raw text becomes model input.

solution.code: Whether the tokenizer preserves or splits those domain-specific strings usefully.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Token boundaries can alter the representation of identifiers and specialized terms.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Inspect examples and compare tokenization choices on held-out data before changing the model.

challenges.title: Respecting permitted context
challenges.description: A text generation model must not use future tokens to predict the next token. Which mechanism enforces this?

choices.text: A tokenizer sorts tokens alphabetically.
A classifier trains on the complete answer before each prediction.
A larger vocabulary reveals future words.
A causal attention mask blocks access to later positions.

challenges.hint: Focus on preventing attention to disallowed positions.

solution.code: A causal attention mask blocks access to later positions.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Without a mask, training could expose tokens unavailable at prediction time.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A causal mask restricts next-token prediction to current and preceding positions.

challenges.title: Finding weakness hidden by aggregate NLP score
challenges.description: A model has high benchmark accuracy but performs poorly on dialect-specific queries. What evaluation is useful next?

choices.text: Report performance on relevant dialect and task slices using representative held-out examples.
Report the overall average again with more decimal places.
Remove dialect labels so subgroup errors cannot be counted.
Tune repeatedly on final test examples.

challenges.hint: An average can hide systematic differences across groups.

solution.code: Report performance on relevant dialect and task slices using representative held-out examples.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A high aggregate score does not establish robustness for every dialect.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Slice-based held-out evaluation locates errors without contaminating the final test.

challenges.title: Choosing an NLP metric for the task
challenges.description: A translation must preserve a safety condition, not exact wording. What is the strongest evaluation?

choices.text: Use exact string match alone because valid translations use identical words.
Use task-specific checks for required meaning and safety alongside suitable text-quality measures.
Count tokens and treat longer output as safer.
Measure training accuracy regardless of deployed outputs.

challenges.hint: Choose measures that reflect the required outcome, not only surface similarity.

solution.code: Use task-specific checks for required meaning and safety alongside suitable text-quality measures.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Valid phrasings can differ while preserving meaning; fluent output can still omit a constraint.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Evaluate semantic preservation and safety conditions on reviewed examples, not just exact wording.

challenges.title: Avoiding leakage in text fine-tuning
challenges.description: Near-duplicate customer messages occur in both training and validation. Why can validation performance mislead?

choices.text: Duplicates guarantee broader language learning.
Validation is misleading only for image datasets.
The model may see nearly identical examples during training and validation, overstating generalization.
Duplicates make class labels unnecessary.

challenges.hint: Check whether splits separate independent examples rather than rows.

solution.code: The model may see nearly identical examples during training and validation, overstating generalization.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Near duplicates can make memorization appear to be generalization.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Group related messages before splitting and retain a separate final test set.

challenges.title: Measuring predicted region overlap
challenges.description: A segmentation model outputs a mask for a damaged surface. Which comparison directly measures overlap with a reference mask?

choices.text: The number of image filenames in the dataset.
The average class label encoded as an integer.
The latency of the image upload request.
Intersection over union between the predicted and reference pixel regions.

challenges.hint: Compare the predicted pixels with the corresponding reference pixels.

solution.code: Intersection over union between the predicted and reference pixel regions.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A region-overlap measure accounts for both shared area and disagreement.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Intersection over union summarizes the overlap relative to the combined predicted and reference regions.

challenges.title: Choosing boxes for object locations
challenges.description: A warehouse camera should return the category and rectangular location of every package. Which task is appropriate?

choices.text: Object detection that predicts class labels and bounding boxes.
Segmentation that outputs only one image-level category.
Regression of one scalar for the entire scene.
Text token classification over package names.

challenges.hint: The required output has multiple objects and coarse rectangular locations.

solution.code: Object detection that predicts class labels and bounding boxes.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Whole-image classification cannot indicate where each package is.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Object detection identifies instances and their bounding boxes.

challenges.title: Using label-preserving augmentation
challenges.description: A traffic model is trained with horizontal flips even where left-versus-right lane markings determine the label. What should the team do?

choices.text: Keep every flip because more augmentation is always beneficial.
Use flips only if they preserve label meaning, or exclude them for this task.
Change labels randomly after each flip.
Apply flips only to validation and test images.

challenges.hint: An augmentation is valid only when the target remains correct after transformation.

solution.code: Use flips only if they preserve label meaning, or exclude them for this task.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A left-right transformation can change a direction-sensitive label.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Choose transformations justified by the task and verify their effect on labels and held-out performance.

challenges.title: Testing a changed camera domain
challenges.description: A defect detector moves from a bright factory camera to a dim camera with different color response. What evaluation tests deployment risk?

choices.text: Reuse the old test score because both datasets contain defects.
Evaluate only on original-camera training images.
Measure performance on representative labeled images from the new camera and lighting.
Change class definitions to match new colors.

challenges.hint: Test under the conditions that changed.

solution.code: Measure performance on representative labeled images from the new camera and lighting.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Lighting and camera response can shift inputs even when task labels remain the same.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A representative target-domain evaluation reveals whether the model remains useful after the move.

challenges.title: Checking labels before model changes
challenges.description: A segmentation model misses thin cracks, but annotators disagree whether cracks count. What is the best first action?

choices.text: Increase model size until disagreement disappears.
Treat each annotator as a separate pixel class without review.
Remove difficult images from evaluation without documenting it.
Clarify and audit the annotation policy and labels before blaming the model alone.

challenges.hint: Check whether the target itself is consistently defined.

solution.code: Clarify and audit the annotation policy and labels before blaming the model alone.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Inconsistent ground truth obscures the difference between model errors and label differences.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Review disagreements and establish a consistent rule before comparing model changes.

challenges.title: Separating primary metrics from robustness tests
challenges.description: A team wants comparable primary metrics for candidate vision models and also wants to test robustness to color and crop changes. Which evaluation design is sound?

choices.text: Use fixed, representative validation and test inputs for primary metrics, and report transformed-input robustness tests separately.
Randomly transform primary validation and test images anew each run, then mix those scores with the primary metrics.
Use only transformed test cases as the primary estimate regardless of deployment conditions.
Apply different transformations to each model primary test set and compare those scores directly.

challenges.hint: Keep the main comparison consistent while allowing a separate stress test.

solution.code: Use fixed, representative validation and test inputs for primary metrics, and report transformed-input robustness tests separately.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Primary model comparisons require the same fixed and representative validation and test examples.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A separate transformed-input suite can test robustness without conflating those results with the primary metrics.

challenges.title: Optimizing a sequence of rewards
challenges.description: A robot gets a small reward for moving toward a goal and a larger reward for finishing safely. Why assess the full reward sequence?

choices.text: Reinforcement learning ignores rewards after the first action.
The policy aims to maximize cumulative reward, so isolated immediate rewards can misrepresent its objective.
The largest immediate reward always gives the best long-term behavior.
Cumulative reward is a supervised class label.

challenges.hint: Consider how actions affect later states and outcomes.

solution.code: The policy aims to maximize cumulative reward, so isolated immediate rewards can misrepresent its objective.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A locally attractive action can lead to worse outcomes later.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Cumulative reward assesses the sequence of consequences the policy is designed to optimize.

challenges.title: Balancing exploration and exploitation
challenges.description: An agent repeatedly chooses a familiar action that gives a modest reward, although an unfamiliar action may lead to a better outcome. What learning challenge is present?

choices.text: The agent is maximizing a supervised loss over labeled actions.
The agent has already proved the unfamiliar action is unsafe.
The agent may be exploiting known rewards too much and exploring too little.
The reward is irrelevant because policies do not use feedback.

challenges.hint: Consider the tradeoff between using known outcomes and learning about alternatives.

solution.code: The agent may be exploiting known rewards too much and exploring too little.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Repeatedly selecting a known modest option can prevent discovering better actions.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Exploration gathers information about alternatives; exploitation uses what is already known.

challenges.title: Constraining exploration in a real system
challenges.description: An agent learns to control a costly machine, and exploratory actions can damage it. What is the safest plan?

choices.text: Allow unrestricted exploration because failures always improve reward.
Train on the machine with no stop condition.
Remove safety limits until the policy converges.
Use a simulator or bounded supervised trials before constrained real-world exploration.

challenges.hint: Account for the cost of exploration, not only its learning benefit.

solution.code: Use a simulator or bounded supervised trials before constrained real-world exploration.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Actions harmless in a game may damage real equipment.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Simulation and explicit operational bounds reduce risk while behavior is evaluated.

challenges.title: Evaluating a learned policy
challenges.description: A policy has high average training reward but occasionally fails badly from a new starting state. What should evaluation include?

choices.text: Representative starting states and inspection of failures, not only mean reward.
Only the best training episode.
Average reward from one familiar starting state.
A claim rare failures do not matter because the mean is high.

challenges.hint: Check variability and tail outcomes across conditions.

solution.code: Representative starting states and inspection of failures, not only mean reward.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A strong average can conceal severe failures in some states.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Evaluate varied held-out scenarios and examine unsafe episodes before deployment.

challenges.title: Distinguishing rewards from labels
challenges.description: A delivery simulator rewards an agent after each route action instead of supplying a correct action label per state. Which setup is this?

choices.text: Supervised learning with complete action labels.
Reinforcement learning from environment feedback and reward.
Unsupervised image segmentation.
A pretrained language model doing retrieval.

challenges.hint: Notice whether feedback is reward from interaction or a supplied target label.

solution.code: Reinforcement learning from environment feedback and reward.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: The agent receives feedback through actions and resulting environment states.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Interaction and reward define the reinforcement-learning setup described.

challenges.title: Understanding a policy
challenges.description: A robot receives the same sensor state twice but chooses different actions because its learned policy is stochastic. What does the policy specify?

choices.text: The complete set of correct labels supplied for every state.
A guarantee that the environment gives a positive reward.
How the agent selects or distributes choices over actions for a given state.
The final cumulative score independent of actions.

challenges.hint: Distinguish the agent decision rule from the reward signal and observed score.

solution.code: How the agent selects or distributes choices over actions for a given state.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A policy describes action selection conditioned on the state, and it may allow multiple actions.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: The policy is the behavior rule; reward evaluates outcomes but is not itself the action rule.

challenges.title: Understanding conditioned generation
challenges.description: A writing assistant receives a prompt and generates several summaries. Which description fits generative AI?

choices.text: It can only copy one exact training example.
It guarantees every generated detail is verified.
It assigns one fixed label and never produces content.
It creates content consistent with learned patterns and supplied context.

challenges.hint: Focus on producing content rather than only selecting a label.

solution.code: It creates content consistent with learned patterns and supplied context.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Generative models learn patterns and can create outputs conditioned on a prompt.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Plausibility does not establish accuracy, provenance, or permission to reuse content.

challenges.title: Understanding repeatability in generation
challenges.description: A user expects identical wording each time they submit the same prompt, but the generative assistant sometimes gives different valid responses. What is the best explanation?

choices.text: Generation can produce different sequences consistent with the learned patterns and prompt.
The assistant necessarily changed its training data between requests.
Every wording difference proves the model is malfunctioning.
The prompt guarantees a single fixed response independent of generation settings.

challenges.hint: Distinguish a generative output from a fixed lookup result.

solution.code: Generation can produce different sequences consistent with the learned patterns and prompt.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Generative models can produce multiple plausible continuations for the same context.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Define whether the task requires semantic consistency or exact repeatability, then evaluate that requirement.

challenges.title: Balancing output diversity and usefulness
challenges.description: A creative system produces varied outputs, but most ignore a requested character limit. What evaluation captures the problem?

choices.text: Measure variety only and disregard the limit.
Measure both diversity and adherence to task constraints.
Measure parameter count as a proxy for quality.
Count unique words as complete task success.

challenges.hint: Useful generation must satisfy the request as well as vary.

solution.code: Measure both diversity and adherence to task constraints.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Diverse outputs can still fail a required constraint.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Track constraint adherence separately from diversity to reveal tradeoffs.

challenges.title: Handling generated content provenance
challenges.description: A model produces a paragraph resembling a published passage. What is the responsible next step?

choices.text: Assume all generated passages are free to reuse.
Remove the model name and treat wording as independently authored.
Check provenance and reuse permissions rather than assuming generation grants permission.
Conclude similarity proves retrieval during this request.

challenges.hint: Distinguish how text was generated from whether it may be reused.

solution.code: Check provenance and reuse permissions rather than assuming generation grants permission.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Generation does not establish ownership, provenance, or permission.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Review the suspected source and applicable attribution or licensing rules before reuse.

challenges.title: Reviewing consequential generated output
challenges.description: A system drafts medical explanations, and some drafts omit key caveats. What control is appropriate before sending?

choices.text: Send every fluent draft automatically.
Remove the caveat requirement.
Evaluate only paragraph length.
Require qualified review and test outputs for the required caveats.

challenges.hint: Match review to the consequence of an omission.

solution.code: Require qualified review and test outputs for the required caveats.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Fluency cannot show that every necessary warning is present.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A review process and explicit checks address the identified risk before delivery.

challenges.title: Working within a context window
challenges.description: An assistant summarizes a long archive, but only some documents fit its prompt. What is the main design consideration?

choices.text: Select and organize relevant context rather than assuming the model sees the entire archive.
Assume every model processes unlimited context.
Replace the prompt with the desired summary as evidence.
Add irrelevant documents until context is full.

challenges.hint: Focus on what is available to the model at generation time.

solution.code: Select and organize relevant context rather than assuming the model sees the entire archive.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: The model can condition only on content supplied within its available context.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Retrieval or staged summarization can prioritize evidence, but check for omissions.

challenges.title: Validating structured LLM output
challenges.description: A downstream service requires an LLM response with exactly three named JSON fields. What should the integration do?

choices.text: Assume valid JSON is guaranteed by a natural-language request.
Validate the generated response against the required schema and handle invalid output explicitly.
Pass any text to the service and let it infer missing fields.
Remove the field requirements after generation.

challenges.hint: Check the boundary between generated text and the consuming software.

solution.code: Validate the generated response against the required schema and handle invalid output explicitly.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A prompt may encourage a format but does not guarantee every output follows it.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Schema validation catches malformed or incomplete responses before downstream use.

challenges.title: Handling irrelevant retrieved passages
challenges.description: A retrieval assistant includes a passage about a different product with a similar name. What should answer generation do?

choices.text: Treat every retrieved passage as correct for every product.
Increase generation temperature until the right passage is selected.
Check passage relevance to the specific question and avoid unsupported details.
Hide retrieved documents from reviewers.

challenges.hint: Retrieved evidence matters only when it matches the query.

solution.code: Check passage relevance to the specific question and avoid unsupported details.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A similar name can retrieve related but incorrect material.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Relevance checks and source-aware review help prevent retrieval errors becoming confident claims.

challenges.title: Understanding tool-enabled answers
challenges.description: One assistant deployment has a calculator tool and another does not. What should evaluators conclude about arithmetic?

choices.text: The model always has calculator access even if disconnected.
A tool call guarantees every value is correct.
Without a tool, the prompt itself proves the result.
Evaluate tool use in the deployment that provides it; fluency alone does not prove calculation.

challenges.hint: Check the capabilities available in the specific product configuration.

solution.code: Evaluate tool use in the deployment that provides it; fluency alone does not prove calculation.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: An LLM can use an external calculator only when the system supplies and invokes one.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Test the integrated path and verify outputs because tool access is no correctness guarantee.

challenges.title: Protecting sensitive prompt information
challenges.description: An employee wants to paste customer medical records into a public chat model. What is the best first response?

choices.text: Check approved data-handling rules and use an authorized privacy-preserving workflow before sharing.
Paste records because summaries cannot reveal sensitive data.
Remove names only and assume all privacy risk is gone.
Ask the public model to promise not to retain data.

challenges.hint: Treat prompt content as data subject to organizational controls.

solution.code: Check approved data-handling rules and use an authorized privacy-preserving workflow before sharing.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Removing names may not remove all sensitive or identifying information.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: An approved workflow defines permitted data, access, retention, and safeguards.

challenges.title: Testing prompt-format robustness
challenges.description: A support assistant succeeds with one template but fails when users phrase the same intent naturally. What should the team do?

choices.text: Report only the successful template.
Evaluate representative prompt variations and improve using held-out formats.
Change expected answers for each failed phrasing.
Assume benchmark score guarantees all phrasings.

challenges.hint: Check whether evaluation covers how users express the same intent.

solution.code: Evaluate representative prompt variations and improve using held-out formats.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A fixed template does not represent the full input distribution.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Held-out prompt formats reveal robustness gaps without tuning on the final test.

challenges.title: Reproducing a trained model
challenges.description: A team finds the deployed model file but cannot identify its training data version or parameters. Which practice addresses this?

choices.text: Keep only the latest model file and delete metadata.
Rely on engineers to remember settings.
Record versioned data references, code, configuration, and model artifacts for each run.
Treat the filename as proof of the complete process.

challenges.hint: Reproduction requires more than the final weight file.

solution.code: Record versioned data references, code, configuration, and model artifacts for each run.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Without data and configuration provenance, a run may not be reconstructable.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Versioning inputs and artifacts makes results traceable and comparable.

challenges.title: Planning a safe model release
challenges.description: A new recommender causes a sharp rise in complaints. What capability helps restore service quickly?

choices.text: Delete all previous model versions.
Immediately overwrite it with an unvalidated retraining job.
Show training accuracy without a serving control.
A tested rollback path to a known prior model version.

challenges.hint: Consider how to reverse a problematic deployment.

solution.code: A tested rollback path to a known prior model version.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A new version can cause harm despite passing pre-release tests.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A retained prior version and tested rollback reduce recovery time.

challenges.title: Catching a changed input schema
challenges.description: A feature pipeline changes timestamps from UTC to local time without notifying the model team. What control can catch this?

choices.text: Automated data-contract or schema checks for expected fields and representations.
A larger network that corrects every timestamp.
Historical training loss only.
Removing timestamp documentation.

challenges.hint: Look for a check at the pipeline-to-serving boundary.

solution.code: Automated data-contract or schema checks for expected fields and representations.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: An unnoticed representation change can make serving inconsistent with training.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Contract checks flag changes for review before the model consumes them.

challenges.title: Interpreting input drift alerts
challenges.description: A dashboard detects changed input distributions, but outcome labels arrive weeks later. What is the sound interpretation?

choices.text: Any input change proves the model is inaccurate.
Drift is a signal to investigate; it does not alone prove predictive performance fell.
No labels proves the model is accurate.
The alert automatically validates a replacement.

challenges.hint: Separate an input signal from measured outcome quality.

solution.code: Drift is a signal to investigate; it does not alone prove predictive performance fell.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Changed inputs may or may not affect performance, and delayed labels limit assessment.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Investigate the change and assess quality when reliable labels mature.

challenges.title: Maintaining ownership in automated release
challenges.description: CI retrains a high-impact eligibility model when new data arrives. Which release process is appropriate?

choices.text: Replace production weights immediately without checks.
Remove owners because automation is responsible.
Keep accountable ownership, review, validation gates, and rollback in the workflow.
Skip validation because training completed.

challenges.hint: Automation should support, not eliminate, release accountability.

solution.code: Keep accountable ownership, review, validation gates, and rollback in the workflow.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A successful training job does not establish that the model is suitable to serve.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Owners and release gates make changes reviewable and recoverable.

challenges.title: Setting a retraining trigger
challenges.description: A model gets daily drift alerts, including harmless seasonal fluctuations. What is a robust response?

choices.text: Retrain after every alert without checking data quality.
Ignore all alerts because some are harmless.
Use original training score as a permanent guarantee.
Define investigation thresholds and retraining criteria using impact and performance evidence.

challenges.hint: A signal should trigger a process, not blindly dictate an update.

solution.code: Define investigation thresholds and retraining criteria using impact and performance evidence.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Drift alerts can include harmless changes and do not identify their cause.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Use documented thresholds and assess data and outcome evidence before retraining.

challenges.title: Understanding data-parallel memory use
challenges.description: A model is too large to fit on one accelerator. The team adds data-parallel workers, but each worker still cannot load the model. Why did this not solve the problem?

choices.text: Data-parallel workers typically keep a model copy, so adding them does not by itself reduce per-worker model memory.
Data parallelism removes all model parameters during training.
More workers automatically compress each model copy.
The model size depends only on the number of training examples.

challenges.hint: Distinguish distributing examples from partitioning model parameters.

solution.code: Data-parallel workers typically keep a model copy, so adding them does not by itself reduce per-worker model memory.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Data parallelism divides batches among workers while each worker trains the same model.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: If the model itself exceeds device memory, replicating it across more workers does not fix that per-device limit.

challenges.title: Diagnosing weak multi-GPU speedup
challenges.description: Adding GPUs barely reduces training time; workers wait during gradient exchange. What likely limits speedup?

choices.text: The model has become a lookup table.
Communication and synchronization overhead.
The validation set is too accurate.
More devices guarantee linear speedup regardless of communication.

challenges.hint: Compare compute time with time spent exchanging updates.

solution.code: Communication and synchronization overhead.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Workers cannot proceed efficiently if communication dominates computation.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Reduce communication cost or change setup, then measure end-to-end throughput.

challenges.title: Diagnosing idle training workers
challenges.description: GPU utilization is low and logs show batches arrive slowly from storage. What should the team investigate?

choices.text: Final accuracy, which controls batch loading speed.
Label names, which determine network bandwidth.
The input pipeline and data loading path, which may be starving accelerators.
More GPUs before checking anything else.

challenges.hint: Find whether compute devices are waiting for data.

solution.code: The input pipeline and data loading path, which may be starving accelerators.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Low utilization with delayed batches points to data input rather than insufficient computation.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Profile loading and preprocessing, then measure whether throughput improves.

challenges.title: Checking batch-size changes
challenges.description: A team adds workers but keeps each worker batch size unchanged, so the global batch grows. Why check training behavior?

choices.text: Weights are guaranteed identical.
A larger batch removes need for validation.
Worker count changes only the run name.
The effective batch and update behavior changed, so the run is not automatically equivalent.

challenges.hint: Count examples contributing to one synchronized update.

solution.code: The effective batch and update behavior changed, so the run is not automatically equivalent.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: More workers processing batches can change examples per update.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Reassess settings and held-out quality when scaling changes training behavior.

challenges.title: Handling a straggling worker
challenges.description: In synchronous distributed training, one worker processes batches much more slowly than the others. What can happen to the shared update cycle?

choices.text: Faster workers may wait for the slow worker before the synchronized update proceeds.
The slow worker batch is automatically converted into a test set.
All workers switch to unrelated models.
The slow worker makes the other workers finish earlier.

challenges.hint: Consider what synchronization requires before all replicas update together.

solution.code: Faster workers may wait for the slow worker before the synchronized update proceeds.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A synchronized step may need results from each worker before it can continue.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A straggling worker can limit end-to-end training speed even when other devices are underused.

challenges.title: Aligning AutoML selection with the objective
challenges.description: An AutoML search selects the lowest-error model, but the product is judged mainly by catching rare hazardous cases. What should be changed before relying on its ranking?

Use training accuracy even if it ignores rare cases.
Select the model with the most preprocessing steps.

challenges.hint: Model selection can only optimize the objective represented by its metric.

solution.code: Define a selection metric that reflects the required hazardous-case performance, then run the search against that criterion.

steps.explanation: An overall error measure may hide poor performance on rare cases important to the product.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Set and document a task-aligned metric before comparing candidates, then verify the choice on held-out data.

challenges.title: Setting an AutoML search budget
challenges.description: An AutoML job searches indefinitely across models and preprocessing options. What should be defined first?

Never record trial configurations.
A documented search space and compute or time budget.
Guarantee the first candidate is optimal.

challenges.hint: Search is a resource-consuming experiment that needs boundaries.

solution.code: A documented search space and compute or time budget.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Unbounded trials consume resources and complicate reproducibility.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A budget and recorded search space make the process manageable.

challenges.title: Reproducing an AutoML result
challenges.description: A winning AutoML model cannot be recreated because only its validation score was saved. What records are needed?

choices.text: Only a screenshot of the best score.
Final test labels inside the model file.
A new random search with no saved settings.
Search configuration, data and split references, selected pipeline, and run settings.

challenges.hint: Ask which inputs and choices determined the model.

solution.code: Search configuration, data and split references, selected pipeline, and run settings.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A score alone does not specify the model or experiment.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Recording the search and data setup makes the result traceable.

challenges.title: Deploying the selected AutoML pipeline
challenges.description: AutoML selects a pipeline that includes imputation, scaling, and a classifier, but deployment exports only the classifier. What is likely to go wrong?

The classifier will automatically reconstruct every preprocessing step.
The model will become a graph neural network.
The validation score will be copied into every prediction.

challenges.hint: Treat preprocessing as part of the selected model pipeline.

solution.code: Serving inputs will skip learned preprocessing and may not match the representation used during model selection.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: AutoML selected transforms determine the features the classifier was trained to consume.

steps.explanation: Export and version the complete preprocessing-and-model pipeline so training and serving use the same transformations.

challenges.title: Keeping preprocessing inside each search fold
challenges.description: An AutoML pipeline scales features on the full dataset before cross-validation. Why can this distort evaluation?

choices.text: Scaling always makes labels incorrect.
Validation-fold information can influence preprocessing statistics used during training.
Cross-validation is valid only for images.
The model cannot optimize numeric features.

challenges.hint: Check whether preprocessing learns values from held-out folds.

solution.code: Validation-fold information can influence preprocessing statistics used during training.

steps.explanation: Statistics computed on all rows expose validation inputs during fitting.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Fit preprocessing inside each training fold to keep each validation fold unseen.

challenges.title: Representing molecules as graphs
challenges.description: A chemistry model predicts a molecule property, and atoms may be listed in different orders for the same molecule. Why use a graph representation?

Use image pixels as the only representation of the molecule.
Nodes and bond edges represent atom identities and connectivity without treating list order as the structure.
Assign a different target property to each atom order.

steps.explanation: A graph encodes atoms and bonds so the model can use relational structure.

challenges.title: Checking graph construction
challenges.description: A molecule graph has atoms as nodes but no bonds as edges. What important information is missing?

Reward assigned to an agent action.
Model output class names.
Connectivity relationships between atoms that describe molecular structure.

challenges.hint: Consider what edges represent in this domain.

solution.code: Connectivity relationships between atoms that describe molecular structure.

steps.explanation: Atoms without bond relationships lose which atoms are connected.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Represent relevant bonds as edges to give message passing molecular neighborhoods.

challenges.title: Avoiding label leakage across graph splits
challenges.description: In node prediction, test nodes connect to training nodes whose labels are input features. What should be checked?

Whether every edge must always be deleted.
Whether test labels should be copied to neighbors.
Whether node features are sorted alphabetically.

solution.code: Whether information crosses the split that would be unavailable in deployment.

steps.explanation: Use an evaluation boundary matching deployment and exclude labels unavailable at prediction time.

challenges.title: Evaluating a changing network

Random splitting is always more realistic than chronological evaluation.

steps.title: Identify the requirement

challenges.title: Recognizing when graph structure matters
challenges.description: A recommender records customers and products they purchased, and shared connections matter. What can a GNN exploit beyond isolated rows?

A guarantee that connected customers have identical preferences.
Neighborhood relationships among customers, products, and their links.
Labels from future purchases.

challenges.hint: Ask whether relationships themselves carry task information.

steps.explanation: An isolated row may omit which entities are linked through purchases.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Message passing can incorporate neighborhoods while evaluation prevents future interactions leaking.

challenges.title: Combining text and image evidence
challenges.description: A product assistant must determine whether an item matches a written description. Why use a multimodal model?

steps.explanation: Text alone cannot verify appearance; an image alone lacks the written claim.

steps.explanation: A multimodal model can align both inputs, with tests for missing or conflicting data.

challenges.title: Accounting for modality reliability
challenges.description: A multimodal assistant receives a blurry product photo and a clear description. What should the system avoid?

Assume blur improves the visual evidence.
Return a confident visual match without acknowledging uncertainty.

steps.explanation: A blurry image may provide weak evidence even when its paired text is clear.

challenges.title: Checking image-text pair alignment

steps.explanation: A mismatched pair is different from a missing modality and can create misleading combined evidence.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Pair-alignment tests check whether the system responds to cross-modal consistency.

challenges.title: Detecting one modality overpowering another
challenges.description: A multimodal classifier barely changes when text changes, though text should alter the decision. What should be investigated?

Whether labels should be removed from evaluation.
Whether the image branch dominates and the model ignores useful text.
Whether the model memorized test answers through text.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Insensitivity to meaningful text changes suggests text may not influence prediction.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Modality ablations and counterfactual pairs measure whether each input contributes appropriately.

challenges.title: Minimizing multimodal data exposure
challenges.description: A service combines faces in photos with names and location text. What privacy consideration follows?

choices.text: Fusion automatically anonymizes images and text.
Privacy controls are unnecessary if accuracy is high.
Removing output labels removes input information.
Combined inputs can reveal more identifying information and need careful controls.

challenges.hint: Consider whether inputs create additional identifying context together.

solution.code: Combined inputs can reveal more identifying information and need careful controls.

steps.explanation: A face, name, and location can identify more strongly in combination.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Limit data to what is needed and apply access, retention, and privacy safeguards.

challenges.title: Validating quantization quality

Measure file size only and ignore defect recall.
Increase test labels until outputs match.

challenges.hint: Judge optimization by task quality as well as resource use.

solution.code: Measure quality on representative cases and adjust or reject quantization if loss is unacceptable.
