steps.explanation: Lower precision can affect predictions, especially on difficult cases.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Benchmark errors on representative data before accepting memory savings.

challenges.title: Understanding pruning
challenges.description: A team removes selected low-importance connections from a neural network to reduce its size. Which technique is this?

choices.text: Quantization.
Pruning.
Retrieval augmentation.
Data parallelism.

challenges.hint: Focus on removing model parts rather than changing numeric precision or data.

solution.code: Pruning.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Pruning removes parameters or connections judged less useful.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Measure model size, latency, and task quality to determine whether pruning helped.

challenges.title: Understanding model distillation
challenges.description: A compact model is trained to imitate outputs from a larger teacher model. Which technique is used?

choices.text: Image segmentation.
Gradient aggregation.
Knowledge distillation.
Subword tokenization.

challenges.hint: The smaller model learns behavior from a larger reference model.

solution.code: Knowledge distillation.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Distillation transfers useful output behavior from teacher to student.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: The student still needs independent evaluation because imitation does not guarantee equal performance.

challenges.title: Benchmarking on deployment hardware
challenges.description: A compressed model is faster on a workstation but slower on the target mobile device. What should guide the decision?

choices.text: Use workstation benchmarks because hardware does not affect inference speed.
Count compression steps regardless of results.
Use training score without deployment measurements.
Measure latency, memory, and quality on the actual target hardware.

challenges.hint: Optimization depends on the device executing the model.

solution.code: Measure latency, memory, and quality on the actual target hardware.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Different hardware handles operations and numerical precision differently.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Use target-device benchmarks for the relevant quality, memory, and tail-latency requirements.

challenges.title: Meeting multiple optimization goals
challenges.description: Pruning meets the memory limit but creates unacceptable tail latency. What is the correct conclusion?

choices.text: The optimization misses a deployment requirement and needs more measurement or a different tradeoff.
Meeting one constraint proves production readiness.
Tail latency can be ignored if average latency is low.
Pruning guarantees lower latency on every device.

challenges.hint: Check requirements independently rather than treating compression as one score.

solution.code: The optimization misses a deployment requirement and needs more measurement or a different tradeoff.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A memory improvement does not imply a latency improvement.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Accept a model only after it meets quality, memory, and latency targets on target hardware.

challenges.title: Scoping an impact assessment
challenges.description: A hospital plans an AI tool to prioritize patient follow-up. What should an impact assessment identify before launch?

choices.text: Only model architecture and parameter count.
Affected groups, plausible harms, mitigations, and accountable owners.
One average accuracy score with no description of users.
A promise that automation prevents harm.

challenges.hint: Start from who may be affected and how decisions could cause harm.

solution.code: Affected groups, plausible harms, mitigations, and accountable owners.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Patients and staff may face different consequences from the deployment.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: An impact assessment makes risks and mitigation ownership explicit before release.

challenges.title: Choosing context for fairness assessment
challenges.description: A hiring model is reviewed using one fairness statistic, but stakeholders disagree about which errors matter most. What is the sound next step?

choices.text: Declare fairness from the single statistic without discussing impacts.
Choose whichever metric gives the most favorable result.
Define the relevant harms and decision context with affected stakeholders before selecting and interpreting fairness measures.
Remove subgroup analysis because metrics can disagree.

challenges.hint: A numerical measure needs a reasoned link to the decision and its consequences.

solution.code: Define the relevant harms and decision context with affected stakeholders before selecting and interpreting fairness measures.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Different error types can impose different harms in a hiring context.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Document the context and affected groups, then interpret suitable measures rather than treating one number as proof.

challenges.title: Providing recourse for affected users
challenges.description: A person is denied an opportunity by an automated score and cannot challenge incorrect input data. What improvement is relevant?

choices.text: Raise the threshold without notifying anyone.
Remove complaint records.
Tell users automated decisions cannot contain errors.
Provide a clear explanation path and a way to correct data or request meaningful human review.

challenges.hint: Consider whether affected people can understand and contest a consequential result.

solution.code: Provide a clear explanation path and a way to correct data or request meaningful human review.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Without correction or review, errors are difficult to address.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Defined recourse supports accountability when relevant information is wrong.

challenges.title: Applying data minimization
challenges.description: A model team wants precise location history though coarse region is sufficient. Which choice reflects privacy-conscious design?

choices.text: Collect and retain only location detail needed for the stated purpose.
Collect all detail in case it becomes useful later.
Share raw histories broadly to speed development.
Assume removing names makes precise locations non-sensitive.

challenges.hint: Ask whether each collected field is necessary.

solution.code: Collect and retain only location detail needed for the stated purpose.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: More precise location creates exposure without a stated need.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Minimization reduces unnecessary collection and pairs with access and retention controls.

challenges.title: Communicating model limitations
challenges.description: A customer-facing model performs poorly on a documented input group. What should deployment do?

choices.text: Call it universally reliable because average score is strong.
Communicate the limitation and set safeguards or alternate handling for affected cases.
Hide the limitation from users and operators.
Assume documentation alone fixes the performance gap.

challenges.hint: Transparency should affect use, not merely document claims.

solution.code: Communicate the limitation and set safeguards or alternate handling for affected cases.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: An average score does not erase known weaknesses for a group.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Disclosure with practical safeguards helps avoid relying on the model outside demonstrated capability.

challenges.title: Assigning accountability
challenges.description: A team says no one owns a harmful model decision because many vendors and internal groups contributed. What governance step is needed?

choices.text: Leave responsibility undefined because several groups participated.
Make the model itself the only accountable party.
Assign a clear accountable owner and responsibilities across the lifecycle.
Remove incident escalation.

challenges.hint: A multi-team system still needs an identifiable decision owner.

solution.code: Assign a clear accountable owner and responsibilities across the lifecycle.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Distributed contributions do not eliminate responsibility when harm occurs.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Named owners and escalation paths support review and mitigation.

challenges.title: Maintaining contracts across stages
challenges.description: A serving service expects a feature in meters, but upstream begins sending centimeters. Which practice helps prevent silent failure?

choices.text: Assume the model infers units from the name.
Change labels after predictions.
Monitor server uptime only, not input meaning.
Define and validate a feature contract, including units, at the pipeline-serving boundary.

challenges.hint: Trace what each component expects at handoff.

solution.code: Define and validate a feature contract, including units, at the pipeline-serving boundary.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: A numeric field with changed units remains syntactically valid but becomes semantically wrong.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Contracts and checks make representation changes visible before predictions are corrupted.

challenges.title: Handling delayed feedback
challenges.description: A deployed ranking model receives reliable outcome labels only after several weeks. How should the team monitor meanwhile?

choices.text: Track available input and service signals, then assess outcome quality when delayed labels mature.
Treat missing immediate labels as proof of perfect performance.
Retrain daily using unlabeled predictions as correct outcomes.
Discard monitoring until labels arrive.

challenges.hint: Separate observable operational signals from delayed measures of task success.

solution.code: Track available input and service signals, then assess outcome quality when delayed labels mature.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Missing outcome labels cannot establish whether ranking is effective.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Monitor what is observable and analyze performance with properly matured labels.

challenges.title: Assigning response to an alert
challenges.description: A dashboard flags malformed inputs, but no team is assigned to investigate. What is missing?

choices.text: A larger training dataset from last year.
An operational owner and response procedure for the monitoring alert.
A model layer that ignores malformed data.
A more complex offline benchmark.

challenges.hint: A signal is useful only if someone can interpret and act on it.

solution.code: An operational owner and response procedure for the monitoring alert.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: An alert without ownership does not ensure the issue is investigated.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Define who triages the alert, what evidence they check, and how service recovers.

challenges.title: Rolling out a model change safely
challenges.description: A new model passes offline checks, but its behavior in production remains uncertain. Which rollout plan limits exposure while gathering evidence?

choices.text: Replace the old version everywhere and delete it immediately.
Avoid monitoring because offline tests passed.
Release to a limited portion of traffic, monitor defined outcomes, and retain a tested rollback path.
Route only known difficult cases to the new model without tracking results.

challenges.hint: Plan for uncertainty after deployment, not just before it.

solution.code: Release to a limited portion of traffic, monitor defined outcomes, and retain a tested rollback path.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Offline results may not capture every production condition or integration effect.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A staged rollout with monitoring and rollback limits risk while collecting operational evidence.

challenges.title: Tracing a prediction end to end
challenges.description: A user disputes a prediction, and the team needs to identify its source record and model. What capability is essential?

choices.text: A dashboard showing only aggregate accuracy.
A random identifier unrelated to data or model versions.
Deleting logs immediately after prediction.
Traceable lineage linking input, transformations, model version, and prediction.

challenges.hint: Debugging requires following the prediction through contributing stages.

solution.code: Traceable lineage linking input, transformations, model version, and prediction.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: Without input and model lineage, the team cannot reconstruct what produced the result.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: Versioned records and traceable transformations support investigation and correction.

challenges.title: Escalating out-of-scope cases
challenges.description: A deployed model receives an input type excluded from evaluation and known to be unreliable. What should the system do?

choices.text: Detect the out-of-scope case and route it to a safe fallback or qualified human review.
Return a confident prediction because every input must receive one.
Add it to training automatically and accept the current answer.
Disable monitoring so the input cannot be detected.

challenges.hint: Use reliability evidence and the system boundary to guide handling.

solution.code: Detect the out-of-scope case and route it to a safe fallback or qualified human review.

steps.title: Identify the requirement
steps.explanation: The model has not been shown to perform reliably on this input type.

steps.title: Apply the course idea
steps.explanation: A fallback or review path prevents unsupported predictions being treated as trustworthy.
